5 Claude Code features that quietly changed how you ship.

Most people are still using Claude Code like fancy autocomplete. These 5 features are the difference between “AI helps me code” and “AI runs my dev loop.”

Checkpoints. Bad refactor? Press Esc twice. It rewinds your code and the chat to any earlier point. Your undo button just got infinite.

Agent fleets. One prompt and Claude writes a script that dispatches dozens of agents to audit your whole repo in parallel. You keep working while 24 agents scan.

Plugin search. Type /plugin and install a whole toolkit (skills, agents, commands, hooks) in one command. 20 tools, one Enter.

Background jobs. Prefix with ! and your dev server plus tests run in the background while Claude keeps editing. No more waiting.

Fallback models. Set a backup chain and Claude keeps shipping when your main model is overloaded. Never get blocked again.

The terminal isn’t a tool anymore. It’s a team.

Google just satisfied the one thing every other AI tool is missing.

A personal agent that runs 24/7 on the cloud. Not your laptop. Not your browser. Their servers.

It’s called Gemini Spark.

Here’s what it actually does and why it matters.

It connects to your entire Google Workspace. Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, Drive, Slides.

You tell it what to do in plain English. Then you close your laptop. It keeps working.

No API keys. No code. No node builders. No terminal.

It comes with a Daily Brief. Every morning it scans your inbox and calendar, then gives you a prioritized summary with next steps.

It has something called Skills. You teach it how you work once and it remembers forever. Like a “ghostwriter” skill that learns your email tone from your last 50 sent messages.

It has Schedules. Set it to run tasks on repeat. Weekly reports, monthly invoices, daily inbox triage. All hands free.

It also connects to third party tools through MCP. Canva, OpenTable, and Instacart at launch. More coming fast.

The tool access is what makes this different. It plugs in through actual APIs, not screen reading or browser hacks. That means faster, more reliable, and more predictable results.

Build these first if you get access:

Weekly inbox recap with a prioritized to do list

Auto invoice generation from a Google Sheet

Lead capture workflow from inbound emails to a tracker

A ghostwriter skill for your most common messages

This is the simplest AI agent setup I’ve seen. Period.

Most people use Codex wrong.

They open a blank chat, type “fix my app,” and wonder why it touches 17 files.

Here’s the 5-step system that actually ships clean code 👇

→ Start inside your repo (not a blank tab)

→ Point at exact files with @mentions

→ Use /plan BEFORE it edits anything

→ Inspect with /diff + /review before shipping

→ Give real bug repros, not “it’s broken”

That’s it.

Do these 5 things and Codex feels like cheating.
Skip them and you’ll fight autocomplete forever.

I wrote a full beginner’s guide breaking down every step (with examples, prompts, and a cheat sheet).
